statements.text: The world has not yet seen a major AI-driven cyber attack. On the scale of attacks like NotPetya or WannaCry, what is the likelihood that we see an attack on this scale or worse in the next 5 years?
statements.context: House hearing titled "Advancing Innovation (Ai): Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Defend and Secure the Homeland," where a member questions an expert panel.

statements.text: Trump's own Department of Justice has warned that China is seeking to become the AI leader by 2030 and plans to use AI chips to modernize its military, design and test weapons of mass destruction, and deploy advanced surveillance tools.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Shri Thanedar at a House subcommittee hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity.

statements.text: You know, I remain deeply worried and concerned about President Trump's decision to allow export of advanced chips to China. [...] who can then use this technology to attack us? Who could use this technology to cyber attack our critical infrastructure?
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity, during the member questioning portion.
